outcome: Still open on 11 Oct 2026: no source claims a proof of the full conjecture, but since 26 Jan 2024 there are restricted cube-centred non-existence results (Chan 2025, She 2025, Ma Aug 2026 preprint), an unrefereed Zenodo claim closing two mixed cube-centred shape families (Yüksel Sayim, first version 12 Jun 2026, AI-assisted per its authors), and an arXiv Lean kernel verification that no such triple exists with n+2 at most 10^12 or 10^14 (Mian and Siddique, 29 Jul 2026, which credits 'Claude (Anthropic)').
problem_asks: The Wikipedia bullet reads 'no three consecutive numbers are all powerful'. Parts: (1) For every positive integer n, at least one of n, n+1, n+2 is not powerful; equivalently there is no n with n, n+1 and n+2 all powerful. 'Powerful' is the usual notion: every prime dividing the number divides it at least squared. There is one part, with no parameters, no counts and no bounds. The claim quantifies over all n, so instance checks up to any finite bound do not settle part (1). Nothing else is asked.

events.what_happened: Trudgian (2016), as cited secondhand in a search snippet of a 2019 paper on Baker's explicit abc conjecture: assuming the explicit abc conjecture, t < 10^20000 for any triple (t-1, t, t+1) of consecutive powerful integers. The original Trudgian paper and the cited hrj.episciences article were not readable here, so the venue and exact wording are not confirmed.
events.delivers: Conditional on the explicit abc conjecture only: a bound t < 10^20000 on the middle term of any consecutive powerful triple. Unconditionally, nothing.
events.direction: A conditional bound on any counterexample. It supports the conjecture only indirectly.

events.what_happened: R. A. Mollin and P. G. Walsh, 'On powerful numbers', Int. J. Math. Math. Sci. 9(4) (1986), 801–806 (DOI 10.1155/S0161171286000984), with a companion note 'A note on powerful numbers, quadratic fields and the Pellian', C. R. Math. Rep. Acad. Sci. Canada 8 (1986), 109–114 (both cited in Chan 2025). They state and give numerical evidence for the no-three-consecutive-powerful-numbers conjecture and show that a triple exists if and only if a Pell-type condition holds (a squarefree m ≡ 7 mod 8 with a fundamental-unit condition). Read only from search snippets and secondary citations: the EMIS PDF returned HTTP 503.
events.delivers: An equivalence: a consecutive powerful triple exists if and only if a Pell-type condition on a squarefree m ≡ 7 (mod 8) holds. Numerical evidence supporting non-existence. No triple excluded.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture (numerical evidence; reduction to a Pell-type condition). No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Edward Beckon, 'On Consecutive Triples of Powerful Numbers', Rose-Hulman Undergraduate Mathematics Journal 20(2) (2019). If a consecutive triple of powerful numbers exists, its smallest member is congruent to 7, 27 or 35 (mod 36). The paper was opened through the Rose-Hulman landing page, which gives the abstract summary.
events.delivers: A necessary congruence restriction on the smallest member of a hypothetical triple (mod 36). Excludes no triple outright.

checked_by.qualification: Undergraduate journal that published the paper in Vol. 20, Iss. 2. Its refereeing practice was not verified.

events.direction: A restriction on a hypothetical counterexample. It cuts toward the conjecture, since it excludes nothing.

events.what_happened: Tsz Ho Chan, 'A note on three consecutive powerful numbers', arXiv:2503.21485 (v1 27 Mar 2025, the only arXiv version seen). Theorem 1: there are no three consecutive powerful numbers of the form x^3−1 = p^3·y^2, x^3, x^3+1 = q^3·z^2 with p, q prime. Corollary 1: 64x^6−1 = p^3·q^3·y^2 has no solution in integers with p, q prime. Method: Pell equations, elliptic curves (integral points computed in SageMath), second-order recurrences. The introduction states the abc-conditional finiteness and calls Conjecture 1 'very hard'. The arXiv journal reference gives Integers 25 (2025), Paper No. A7, 7 pp.
events.revisions: v1 27 Mar 2025 only on the arXiv page read; journal version Integers 25 (2025) A7 per the arXiv journal reference.
events.delivers: A restricted case: cube-centred triples (x^3−1, x^3, x^3+1) in which both outer terms have the form prime-cubed times a square. Nothing else.
events.remains: All of part (1): the general claim, cube-centred triples with other outer shapes, and all middle terms that are not cubes.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal that published the note. Refereeing practice not verified.
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the note as Paper A7 in Integers 25 (2025), per the arXiv journal reference

events.directly_checkable: The proof is by hand, with SageMath used to compute integral points on elliptic curves. No certificate file was identified in the sources read.
events.direction: Proves a restricted non-existence case, consistent with the conjecture. No object exhibited.
people: Tsz Ho Chan (Kennesaw State University, per search snippet)

events.what_happened: Jialai She, 'Nonexistence of consecutive powerful triplets around cubes with prime-square factors', arXiv:2507.16828 (v1 7 Jul 2025; v2 24 Jul 2025; v3 24 Sep 2025). Theorem 1: there exist no consecutive powerful numbers of the form x^3−1 = p^2·a^3, x^3, x^3+1 = q^2·b^3 with p, q prime. Method: modular arithmetic, p-adic valuation, Thue equations, elliptic curves. The abstract calls the general conjecture 'a celebrated open problem'. Journal publication as Integers A103, published 25 Nov 2025, is from a search snippet of the journal record; the Integers PDF was not readable here.
events.revisions: v1 7 Jul 2025; v2 24 Jul 2025; v3 24 Sep 2025 (arXiv page). Journal Integers A103, 25 Nov 2025 (search snippet only).
events.delivers: A restricted case: cube-centred triples in which x^3−1 = p^2·a^3 and x^3+1 = q^2·b^3 (prime-squared times cube on both outer terms). Nothing else.
events.remains: All of part (1), cube-centred triples with other outer shapes, and all middle terms that are not cubes.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal that published the paper as A103. Refereeing practice not verified.
checked_by.what_they_did: Published as Integers A103 (25 Nov 2025, per a search snippet of the journal record; not confirmed from the journal page)

events.direction: Proves a restricted non-existence case, consistent with the conjecture. No object exhibited.
people: Jialai She (Phillips Academy, per search snippet)

events.what_happened: Shusei Narumi and Yohei Tachiya, 'On the number of k-full integers between three successive k-th powers', arXiv:2512.07438 (v1 8 Dec 2025; v2 18 Feb 2026). The abstract gives an explicit density for n where intervals between successive k-th powers contain given numbers of k-full integers, and claims infinitely many triples of successive k-th powers in the k-full sequence. A 2026 forum comment on Erdős #938 cites it. It does not concern consecutive integers or the EMW conjecture.
events.delivers: Nothing on the EMW conjecture. It concerns k-full integers between successive k-th powers, a different question from three consecutive powerful integers.
events.direction: Off-target. No bearing on the claim in part (1).

events.what_happened: P. G. Walsh, 'A question of Erdös on 3-powerful numbers and an elliptic curve analogue of the Ankeny-Artin-Chowla conjecture', arXiv:2404.03970 (submitted 5 Apr 2024, one version). The abstract concerns a conjecture of Erdős on 3-powerful numbers via the Mordell–Weil group of an elliptic curve family. It does not mention consecutive numbers or the EMW conjecture. Separately, a Walsh 2024 abstract hosted at ntrg.math.unideb.hu and a 'walsh-2024-preprint' link on the Zagreb site were not readable or returned 404; see incomplete.
events.delivers: Nothing on the EMW conjecture. It concerns 3-powerful numbers, a different question.

events.what_happened: Andreas Reinhart, 'A counterexample to the Pellian equation conjecture of Mordell', arXiv:2402.09827 (v1 15 Feb 2024; v2 11 Jun 2024). The abstract extends the list of squarefree d ≥ 2 for which the fundamental unit has y divisible by d, and gives a counterexample to a conjecture of Mordell. The arXiv abstract page does not mention the EMW conjecture. A search snippet says the introduction refers to it; the PDF text was unreadable here, so this is unresolved.
events.delivers: On the abstract, a counterexample to a Mordell conjecture about fundamental units and divisibility by d. This is topically close to the unit conditions Mollin and Walsh use, but the abstract does not state that it settles or moves part (1).
events.doubts: Whether the paper bears on EMW at all is unresolved: the abstract page does not mention it, while a search snippet says the introduction does. The PDF could not be read to check.
events.direction: Not established. On the abstract it is about a different question.
events.object: A counterexample to a Mordell conjecture on the Pellian equation; the abstract does not describe the object further.

events.what_happened: Wenjun Ma, 'An elementary note on three consecutive powerful numbers', arXiv:2608.23418 (v1 24 Aug 2026). Per the arXiv HTML as read through the fetch tool: Theorem 1.2 states that there are no three consecutive powerful numbers x^n−1 = q1^3·y^2, x^n, x^n+1 = q2^3·z^2 (q1, q2 prime) when n ≥ 5 and every prime factor of x^n lies in S, the primes p ≥ 5 with p ≡ 5 (mod 8). The fetched text says the proof in §3 treats only prime exponents p ≡ 5 (mod 8). The abstract says it extends Chan's cube-centred result to similar cases whose middle term can be a perfect power for infinitely many exponents, using Nagell–Ljunggren, Lebesgue and Ko together with elementary methods. The paper states the EMW conjecture is open. The PDF was not readable.
events.delivers: A restricted case: outer terms of Chan's prime-cubed-times-square shape, with the middle term a perfect power x^n (n ≥ 5, prime factors in S). Nothing outside that.
events.remains: All of part (1), cube-centred triples with other outer shapes, and middle terms outside the S restriction.
events.time_since_posted: about 7 weeks; no engagement found in search
events.doubts: Scope: the stated theorem (composite exponents n ≥ 5 with prime factors in S) appears broader than the case the proof treats (prime exponents p ≡ 5 mod 8). This rests on the fetch tool's reading of the HTML. I did not read the full text myself.
events.direction: A restricted non-existence case, consistent with the conjecture. No object exhibited.

events.what_happened: Wouter van Doorn, 'Three-term arithmetic progressions of consecutive powerful numbers', arXiv:2605.06697 (v1 4 May 2026). Theorem 1: infinitely many three-term arithmetic progressions N, N+d, N+2d of powerful numbers with d = 2√N + 1. Conjectures that infinitely many of these progressions consist of three consecutive terms of the powerful sequence, which is Erdős Problem #938, a different question from consecutive integers. The HTML's AI disclosure says: 'In the making of this paper, ChatGPT was used as a sounding board, for proofreading and for supplying numerical examples', and 'The paper itself was entirely human-generated.'
events.delivers: Infinitely many three-term progressions of powerful numbers. Nothing about three consecutive integers. Nothing on the EMW conjecture.
events.direction: Off-target for part (1). The paper concerns #938.

events.what_happened: Berkay Yüksel Sayim (independent researcher, Germany), 'Nonexistence of consecutive powerful triplets around cubes with mixed prime factorizations', self-deposited on Zenodo. Versions: v1.0 (record 20654530), published 12 Jun 2026; v1.1 (21174127), 3 Jul 2026, editorial only; v1.2 (22648658), 7 Sep 2026, disclosure revision and one overview figure; v1.3 (22699364, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22699364), 11 Sep 2026, citation correction. The Zenodo description says the note rules out the two remaining mixed families: no consecutive triple with x^3−1 = p^2·a^3 and x^3+1 = q^3·z^2, nor with x^3−1 = p^3·y^2 and x^3+1 = q^2·b^3. Both reduce to t^6+t^3+1 = 3w^2, solved via a rank-0 elliptic quotient of a palindromic genus-2 curve, and the note refines Beckon's mod-36 constraint to arbitrary prime-square moduli. The archive includes LaTeX and SymPy/SageMath scripts. On erdosproblems.com (forum comment, 4 Oct 2026, 15:45) the author writes: 'These are partial results and not a solution of #364.' A proof claim on the same site (4 Oct 2026, 19:56:46) says: 'I claim that two mixed forms are impossible for the neighbours of a cube.'
events.revisions: v1.0 12 Jun 2026; v1.1 3 Jul 2026 (editorial, no mathematics changed); v1.2 7 Sep 2026 (disclosure revision and one figure, no mathematics changed); v1.3 11 Sep 2026 (citation correction). The Zenodo API lists v1.3 as the last version of concept 20654529.
events.delivers: Excludes two further mixed shape families for cube-centred triples, which the author describes as closing the remaining mixed cases of the family left by Chan and She. Non-cube middle terms and the general claim are not treated.
events.remains: All of part (1): the general claim, non-cube middle terms, and cube-centred triples outside the two named families.
events.time_since_posted: about 4 months; the erdosproblems proof claim had 0 comments as of 11 Oct 2026
events.directly_checkable: The reduction to t^6+t^3+1 = 3w^2 and the rank-0 elliptic quotient are checkable with computer algebra. The archive contains SymPy and SageMath scripts, which I did not read or run. The PDF is not readable with the tools available.
events.doubts: (a) Not refereed: self-deposited on Zenodo, with no journal or peer review found. (b) The author is an independent researcher with no institutional affiliation, per Zenodo. (c) The authors' own acknowledgement in v1.0 and v1.1 says that substantial parts of the work, including the reduction of Section 5, were developed with AI assistance; the v1.2 disclosure replaced it with a full 'Use of AI tools' section, which I could not read. Section 5 is the reduction on which the mixed cases rest, so the AI input may be load-bearing. (d) The erdosproblems proof claim says the rank-0 step is computer-assisted (SageMath) and has no comments. (e) The claim is restricted to two named families, and the author says so.
events.direction: Excludes two mixed cube-centred shape families. Consistent with the conjecture. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: A forum post by piotrek3421 on erdosproblems.com Problem #938 (26 Sep 2026, 20:55). It reports computations for three-term progressions of consecutive powerful numbers: a search to 10^16 found 31 progressions; a Pell-family analysis with x0 = 11427 and x1 = 2984191388685; and a check of squarefree m ≤ 6·10^6. It opens with 'Some computational data, obtained with AI assistance' and says the code is 'available on request'. This is a forum post, not a preprint, and it concerns #938, not the EMW conjecture.
events.delivers: Nothing on the EMW conjecture. Computational data about #938, a different question.
events.directly_checkable: The code is 'available on request' and was not obtained.

events.what_happened: Ibrahim Mian and Shayaan Siddique (Millennium Research), 'A Kernel-Certified Verification of the Erdős–Mollin–Walsh Conjecture below 10^14', arXiv:2609.25011. The arXiv API gives published and updated 2026-07-29T03:53:11Z, but the ID carries the 2609 stamp, which does not match a July submission. This is unresolved. Two Lean 4 theorems, Erdos364.no_powerful_triple_up_to_1e12 and Erdos364.no_powerful_triple_up_to_1e14, say that no n with n+2 ≤ X has n, n+1 and n+2 all powerful, for X = 10^12 and 10^14. The reduction to odd n uses a mod-4 argument, and the odd powerful numbers come from a kernel-checked generator certified over 3,524 per-interval Boolean certificates. Seven surviving distance-2 pairs are eliminated by explicit witnesses. Lean 4.30.0 and mathlib v4.30.0. The paper reports no sorry and no native_decide, with axioms exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. It says the statement is pinned byte-for-byte to the community formal-conjectures formalisation. Its acknowledgements credit Claude (Anthropic), quoted in ai.
events.revisions: v1 only seen; the arXiv API reports updated equal to published
events.delivers: A finite verification: no three consecutive powerful numbers n, n+1, n+2 with n+2 ≤ 10^12, and likewise with n+2 ≤ 10^14, each checked by the Lean kernel from the standard axioms. Nothing beyond these bounds. The paper says finite verification cannot settle the conjecture.
events.remains: Part (1) for all n above 10^14, which is unbounded. The repository calls it 'the first verification of the conjecture at any finite bound that is checked end to end by a proof kernel', so the novelty is the kernel certification, not the range.
events.time_since_posted: about 11 weeks; no engagement found in search

machine_checked.system: Lean 4.30.0 with mathlib v4.30.0 (proof-kernel check, per the paper)

events.directly_checkable: The Optio repository holds the Lean sources and chunk certificates (Erdos364/C12, Erdos364/C14), with axiom records in data/. A Lean 4.30.0 build would check them. I did not build them and did not confirm the sorry count, so sorry_free rests on the paper's statement.
events.doubts: No peer review and no human reading found. The earlier search bound cited on erdosproblems (no such n below 7.38×10^28, provenance unclear) is larger than 10^14, so this is not a range record. The arXiv ID stamp (2609) conflicts with the 29 Jul 2026 date from the API. The acknowledgement leaves open which parts of the Lean development were AI-written; see ai.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in the stated range: no counterexample with n+2 ≤ 10^14. Nothing cuts against it.
events.object: No object: a kernel-checked nonexistence statement for each bound, obtained from an exhaustive finite enumeration with explicit certificates and seven explicit non-powerfulness witnesses. Not constructive in the sense of exhibiting a triple; it is a finite exhaustive check.

systems.name: Claude (Anthropic)
systems.what_it_did: Not specified. The acknowledgement says only that development was carried out with its assistance. It does not say whether the model wrote the Lean code, the enumeration generator, the certificates or the reduction. The paper says the enumeration technique 'adapts prior in-house work'.
systems.basis_quote: Development was carried out with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic).

events.what_happened: google-deepmind/formal-conjectures, FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/364.lean (Apache 2.0, copyright header 2025). It formalises Erdős Problem 364 with the main theorem erdos_364, ¬∃ n, Powerful n ∧ Powerful (n+1) ∧ Powerful (n+2), tagged 'research open' and left as sorry. The variant erdos_364.variants.strong (Erdős's gap statement) is also sorry. erdos_364.variants.weak (no four consecutive) is proved. Commit dates and authors are not visible on the page.
events.delivers: Nothing: it is a formal statement of the problem with the main claim unproved. It is not progress on part (1).
events.direction: The problem as stated. No direction.
people: The Formal Conjectures authors (Google DeepMind repository)

events.what_happened: A claimed finite search: no n below 7.38×10^28 with n, n+1 and n+2 all powerful. It appears on erdosproblems.com #364 in a forum comment by Yuchen_Li (21 Dec 2025), citing OEIS A076445. The OEIS page I opened (A076445, 'The smaller of a pair of powerful numbers that differ by 2') gives no such bound. Its comments and extensions are from 2002 to 2006, and it cites Mollin and Walsh only in its links. The erdosproblems history shows the cited OEIS number and the bound changing between versions, and one version reads as 'n<8×10^228', garbled. The origin of the 7.38×10^28 figure is unresolved.
events.revisions: erdosproblems history shows versions dated 20 Oct 2025, 13 Apr 2026 and a current undated version, with the OEIS reference and bound changing between them
events.delivers: If correct, a finite search with no such n below 7.38×10^28. No proof and no abc-based argument. Unverified.
events.doubts: The provenance is unresolved. The OEIS page does not carry the bound, and the erdosproblems history shows the cited number and bound changing between versions, including a garbled value of 8×10^228.
events.direction: Finite instances only: no triple below the stated bound. Does not move the conjecture's own quantity.

disputes.summary: Who conjectured it. erdosproblems.com and the Lean file credit Erdős (Manitoba 1976, Eureka 1975/76 in Chan's references) and, independently, Mollin and Walsh (1986). The Prime Pages and some sources add that Golomb raised the question in 1970. This is attribution, not a dispute about the result.

summary:
Nothing since 26 Jan 2024 settles the Erdős–Mollin–Walsh conjecture. It is listed as open in Wikipedia's Powerful number article, which calls it 'a conjecture of Erdős, Mollin, and Walsh', and in erdosproblems.com #364 (history: last edit 13 Apr 2026; the status label was not directly read). The DeepMind formal statement still has erdos_364 as sorry. The events since 2024 fall into three groups. (i) Restricted cube-centred cases. Chan (arXiv 27 Mar 2025; Integers 25 (2025) A7) rules out x^3−1 = p^3·y^2, x^3, x^3+1 = q^3·z^2. She (arXiv 7 Jul 2025; Integers A103 per a snippet) rules out the p^2·a^3 / q^2·b^3 shape. Ma (arXiv 24 Aug 2026; abstract and HTML read, PDF not) extends the cube-type case to middle terms x^n, n ≥ 5, with prime factors in a set S; the proof as fetched covers only prime exponents p ≡ 5 mod 8. Sayim's Zenodo note (first version 12 Jun 2026, latest 11 Sep 2026, no refereeing found) claims the two mixed families left by Chan and She; the author's own forum comment says 'partial results and not a solution of #364'. (ii) A finite Lean verification. Mian and Siddique (arXiv 2609.25011) show by kernel-checked Lean 4 that no triple exists with n+2 ≤ 10^12 and ≤ 10^14, sorry-free per the paper. Their range is below the 7.38×10^28 search that erdosproblems cites from OEIS, whose provenance I could not confirm. (iii) Neighbouring work that is not this question and is recorded as discounted: #938 (three-term progressions, van Doorn, the 26 Sep 2026 forum post by piotrek3421), k-full integers (Narumi–Tachiya), 3-powerful numbers (Walsh 2024), and Reinhart's Mordell-conjecture counterexample (Feb 2024), whose EMW bearing is unresolved. Forum comments on #364 by Alfaiz, Yuchen_Li and marinov are noted but are not events.

AI involvement. Two events name AI in the mathematics. Sayim's acknowledgement, as quoted in the Zenodo v1.2 note, reads 'substantial parts of the work, including the reduction of Section 5, were developed with AI assistance'; the v1.2 'Use of AI tools' section could not be read, and no system is named in any text I could read, so ai.systems is empty rather than filled from elsewhere. Mian and Siddique's acknowledgement reads 'Development was carried out with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic).' This is recorded as 'Claude (Anthropic)', and the paper does not say which parts Claude produced. Chan, She, Ma (HTML), Narumi–Tachiya and Walsh 2024 show no AI mention in what I read. In #938 items, van Doorn discloses ChatGPT for a sounding board, proofreading and numerical examples, and piotrek3421 says 'computational data, obtained with AI assistance'. None of these is on this problem. I found no AI claim on this problem from the lab or tracker side (Astra's reconstructed list of ten results names Erdős 146, 180 and 183, not 364; the full list was not found).

Close calls. (a) Whether Sayim's note moves the problem: the conjecture's own claim is that no triple exists; a non-existence result for a named shape family is a case of that claim, not the claim, but the author's statement that the note 'closes the remaining mixed configurations' of the Chan/She family is a claim about a family, not about part (1). (b) Whether Mian–Siddique moves a bound: it adds finite instances, which by the DEEP_DIVE scope rule do not change the conjecture's quantity, and it does not beat the 7.38×10^28 figure. (c) Whether the AI input is load-bearing: Sayim's Section 5 reduction is what the mixed cases depend on, which suggests it is, but 'developed with AI assistance' does not say the model produced the argument. The Mian–Siddique 'development' sentence does not say what Claude produced, and the paper says the enumeration technique adapts prior in-house work. (d) Whether Ma's stated theorem exceeds its proof: read from the fetch tool's summary of the HTML, not from my own reading of the full text.

Discrepancies. Mian's arXiv ID carries the stamp 2609, but the API reports 29 Jul 2026. Sayim's Zenodo DOI appears as 20654529 in the forum link (the concept record) and 22699364 for v1.3. The She arXiv abstract page gives no conjecture on x^n−1 being never powerful, although a search summary said so; I did not find it in the HTML. The OEIS A076445 page does not carry the 7.38×10^28 bound. The Walsh 2024 abstract and the Reinhart PDF were unreadable here, so their links to EMW are unresolved.
competing_reading: Read the Sayim note and the Mian–Siddique verification as the real movement in the window. Sayim's note closes two named mixed families of the cube-centred case, and the authors credit AI with 'the reduction of Section 5', which the mixed cases rest on. Mian–Siddique is the first kernel-checked verification below 10^14, and the authors credit 'Claude (Anthropic)' with development. On that reading both events carry load-bearing AI involvement, and the problem has moved on the restricted cube-centred case. Against it: Sayim's result is unrefereed and self-deposited, its author states it is partial, and it covers two shape families of one restricted case, so it does not change what part (1) asks. Mian–Siddique is a finite check that leaves the unbounded claim open and does not beat the cited 7.38×10^28 search. Its AI sentence does not say what the model produced.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full 'Use of AI tools' section and the theorem statements of Sayim's v1.3 PDF (sayim-2026-emw-mixed-triplets-v13.pdf in Zenodo record 22699364), which the tools here could not read, to see what the AI did and whether a model is named. (2) The Optio repository's commit history and authorship, to see what Claude wrote: the Lean code, the enumeration generator, or the mathematics. (3) A referee report, journal acceptance, or a named expert's check of the §5 elliptic-curve reduction in Sayim's note. (4) Ma's full text (Theorem 1.2 and §3), to see whether the composite exponents are proved. (5) The origin and date of the 7.38×10^28 search bound. (6) The Integers journal pages for She's A103 and Chan's A7, to confirm the dates from snippets.

event.what_happened: Tsz Ho Chan, 'A note on three consecutive powerful numbers', arXiv:2503.21485 (v1 27 Mar 2025, the only arXiv version seen). Theorem 1: there are no three consecutive powerful numbers of the form x^3−1 = p^3·y^2, x^3, x^3+1 = q^3·z^2 with p, q prime. Corollary 1: 64x^6−1 = p^3·q^3·y^2 has no solution in integers with p, q prime. Method: Pell equations, elliptic curves (integral points computed in SageMath), second-order recurrences. The introduction states the abc-conditional finiteness and calls Conjecture 1 'very hard'. The arXiv journal reference gives Integers 25 (2025), Paper No. A7, 7 pp.
event.revisions: v1 27 Mar 2025 only on the arXiv page read; journal version Integers 25 (2025) A7 per the arXiv journal reference.
event.delivers: A restricted case: cube-centred triples (x^3−1, x^3, x^3+1) in which both outer terms have the form prime-cubed times a square. Nothing else.
event.remains: All of part (1): the general claim, cube-centred triples with other outer shapes, and all middle terms that are not cubes.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal that published the note. Refereeing practice not verified.
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the note as Paper A7 in Integers 25 (2025), per the arXiv journal reference

event.directly_checkable: The proof is by hand, with SageMath used to compute integral points on elliptic curves. No certificate file was identified in the sources read.
event.direction: Proves a restricted non-existence case, consistent with the conjecture. No object exhibited.

judgement.why: The statement is one universal claim, so each shape-family non-existence result (Chan, She, Ma, Sayim) is a case; Chan and She are digested via acceptance in Integers, Ma and Sayim are unreviewed and doubtful. Mian–Siddique and the 7.38e28 search are finite checks (instances). Trudgian is conditional on explicit abc (variant); Mollin–Walsh's Pell equivalence and Beckon's congruence exclude nothing (none). #938, k-full, 3-powerful and Mordell-Pellian papers are different questions (variant). AI: Mian–Siddique's sentence 'Development was carried out with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic)' does not say the model produced any mathematics, and the result is instances anyway, so none. Sayim's ai.systems is empty with none_found false; the paraphrased acknowledgement ('reduction of Section 5 ... developed with AI assistance') names no system and does not say a model produced the argument, so none — the closest call in the record.
judgement.doubts: Sayim's AI role could be 'assisted' if the unread v1.2 'Use of AI tools' section shows a model produced the Section 5 reduction; the record could not read it. She's journal acceptance rests on a search snippet of the Integers record. Mian–Siddique's arXiv ID stamp (2609) conflicts with its 29 Jul 2026 API date; immaterial since it is instances. Formal-conjectures date is year-only 2025, safely after the snapshot.
